text.p: Shares in Portuguese utility EDP should open at between 2,700 and 3,000 escudos per share on Tuesday, 20 to 33 percent above the 2,250 escudo privatisation price, as institutional funds snap up shares they failed to obtain in the sell-off, analysts and dealers said.
"EDP could hit 2,850 escudos on the first day of trade, or even 2,900, and everyone will be attacking the tight supply," said an analyst with a domestic broker.
An analyst with a national bank said: "EDP will open at between 2,800 and 2,850 escudos, with very strong demand."
A London dealer said: "2,700 escudos is the lowest trading price that I foresee. The price could go as high as 3,000 escudos."
The dealer said that in the grey market in London EQUITY1, the bid for EDP is around 2,900 escudos and the asking price is around 3,200.
On Monday the government fixed the privatisation price at 2,250 escudos in the sale of 30 percent of the 600 billion escudos capital of EDP.
Demand in the direct sale was about 30 times supply and in the public offer for sale (OPV) more than 37 times.
According to most analysts, EDP shares will rise towards the fundamental value of the company, above 3,000 escudos per share.
"We are convinced that the share will rise sharply. We believe the fundamental value of EDP right now is around 3,100 escudos," said Miguel Sequeira of Banco Finantia.

James Harrison, analyst with Lisbon broker Midas, said: "Our range for the fundamental value of EDP is between 3,000 and 3,250 escudos per share. A valuation of 3,150 escudos per share is based on discount cashflow."
He added: "Theoretically, this level of 3,150 escudos could be reached in the next six months.
He said he expected average growth in earnings per share of around 11 percent per year and average annual growth of nine percent for dividends in the next five years.
One analyst said: "Tomorrow we will see some international and domestic professional investors who have portfolios invested in the PSI20 .PSI20 index (of 20 leading shares) piling into EDP."
EDP shares will be included in the PSI20 index from July 1.
